title: Endpoint locality declaration wizard and attestation bundle export
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Add a guided 'locality declaration' experience when customers create or update a hosted endpoint, plus a backend job that composes a signed attestation bundle (location assertions, retention policy, TTLs, and routing traces) and exposes an export endpoint for audit ingestion. This ticket covers product spec, acceptance criteria, API contract, and rollout plan for a canary release.
acceptance_criteria: Users can declare endpoint location constraints (allowed regions, preferred region, soft/hard locality) during endpoint create/update via the Console wizard and the API.
Declared locality is stored as structured metadata on the endpoint and is visible in the Console endpoint detail page and exportable via the admin API.

Automated attestation bundle generator produces a time-stamped, signed archive (JSON + manifest) that includes: endpoint metadata, effective routing decisions for last 30 days, retention settings, and evidence of any fallback events.
Export endpoint returns a download URL with RBAC checks and an entry in the organization's audit log; bundles can be delivered to customer-configured S3/GCS destinations or downloaded manually.
Canary rollout targets 5 existing customers with no customer-impacting failures and telemetry shows no latency regressions >5% on control plane operations.
E2E tests for API, Console flow, and export job pass in staging and pre-prod environments.
implementation_plan: Product: finalize wizard copy, form fields and validation; define HTTP API schema for locality metadata (JSON schema attached).
Design: create Console mockups for the wizard and endpoint detail; add export action in endpoint actions menu.
Backend: add locality metadata to Endpoint model, migration, validation and index for queries; implement attestation generator service and signed manifest creation.
Routing: annotate request routing logs with endpoint locality tag and normalize traces for inclusion in attestation bundle.
Exports: implement secure presigned URL flow + push-to-s3/gcs option; add export audit record and retention lifecycle for generated bundles.
Testing: unit tests, integration tests for export flow, and chaos tests to validate fallback traces are captured.
Rollout: feature-flagged canary (10% orgs or 5 named orgs), monitoring dashboard for errors, export latencies, and bundle sizes.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Choice: include 30-day routing history in default bundle to balance forensic value vs. bundle size. Can be extended by request.
Tradeoff: signed JSON manifest rather than a full PKI-signed binary to simplify verifier tooling for customers. We will add stronger crypto if customers require HSM-backed signatures.

Decision: allow both hard locality (strict deny outside allowed regions) and soft locality (prefer region but allow fallback with recorded justification); hard locality requires additional SLA/contract gating.
notes_and_updates: 2025-03-13: Kickoff meeting with infra, routing, and security. Key ask from security: ensure attestation bundles are tamper-evident and include a provenance chain. Action: engineering to propose manifest schema.
2025-03-14: Design sketches uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/COMPLIANCE/Endpoint+Locality+Wizard. Designer: Marisol Vega.

2025-03-15: Backend alignment: DB migration planned to add endpoint.locality JSONB and index on organization_id + locality.preferences. Migration PR drafting: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2749.

2025-03-16: Security raised question about PII in routing traces. Decision: redact user-level identifiers and only include service-level routing decisions; record redaction in manifest. Follow-up: create data-minimization checklist.
2025-03-17: QA flagged an edge-case where export job OOMs if routing history >10M lines. Engineering will cap events and provide truncated summary + pointer to raw logs for enterprise bundles.
2025-03-18: Updated acceptance criteria to include delivery to customer-managed buckets and RBAC enforcement on exports.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Large attestation bundles may cause storage and transfer costs. Mitigation: default to compressed JSON (gzip) and 30-day cap; provide config for longer retention for enterprise customers.
Risk: Mis-declared locality could cause regulatory exposure. Mitigation: Add warning copy, validation rules, and an optional review approval workflow for hard locality requests.
Risk: Export endpoint could be abused. Mitigation: require org-level export permission and rate-limit exports; add audit log entries for all exports.
